### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via validateExpression (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx`  _(via validateExpression (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **32** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8bceb6a2c65fe18cbac6560537edea5dd3f8dd6a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2b60d579a6386a3385c9db6aebcc72de2afea8a6` — the merge of head `f8b2897f5de19151231ef9d7c47e028d10fee24c` into base `8bceb6a2c65fe18cbac6560537edea5dd3f8dd6a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2b60d579a6386a3385c9db6aebcc72de2afea8a6 && git checkout 2b60d579a6386a3385c9db6aebcc72de2afea8a6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8bceb6a2c65fe18cbac6560537edea5dd3f8dd6a f8b2897f5de19151231ef9d7c47e028d10fee24c && git checkout -B drift-repro 8bceb6a2c65fe18cbac6560537edea5dd3f8dd6a && git merge --no-ff f8b2897f5de19151231ef9d7c47e028d10fee24c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8bceb6a2c65fe18cbac6560537edea5dd3f8dd6a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8bceb6a2c65fe18cbac6560537edea5dd3f8dd6a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Reviewed at 2026-11-01T15:10Z against merge-base `a06feb76f457c22b751170cb6e30193e4a9d5a26` with origin/main. Inputs read: card #28659, triage 6558290991, claim 6558630190, order-28659.md, os-dev-report 6559671824, the PR body, the head's check-runs, #22019 and #26608.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set, formula field `expression` (narrowed).** A formula whose `label(record.FIELD)` names a declared field with no `options` list is now refused at every face that runs `validateStackExpressions`: `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint` (unit-pinned in the new lint test), the active object save door, draft `_diagnostics` and per-item publish (all three read `judgeRuntimeAuthoringRules`, protocol-authoring-gate.ts:211; drafts stay ungated per D1, runtime-authoring-gate.ts, and `draftPublishVerdict` reads the same verdict) and the history **restore** door (`door: 'restore'`, protocol-authoring-gate.ts:138, which the PR does not list but which runs the same function). Correct against the card's expected behaviour and the order's ruling. One rule id (`expression-invalid`), one message family (`optionlessLabelSentence`, byte-identical to the evaluator's WARN). Correct.
2. **Compound expressions.** The AST walk visits every node, so `label(record.kind) + label(record.first)` and a nested call are refused for `first` alone; one refusal per field (`seen`). Correct.
3. **Unknown field and unregistered function unchanged.** `declared.has(field)` guards the new arm, so an undeclared field keeps its `unknown-field` refusal with no second one; `checkOptionLabelTargets` runs only inside the parse-ok branch after `checkFieldExistence`, so the unregistered-function refusal path is untouched. Pinned by controls in both new suites. Correct.
4. **`@objectstack/formula` public surface (widened, additive).** `ExprSchemaHint.optionFields?: readonly string[]` (optional, opt-in: absent ⇒ no judgment, so every existing caller is unchanged); `declaresOptions` added to the entry; `ExpressionRefusalCode` / `ExpressionRefusalParams` / `EXPRESSION_REFUSAL_CODES` gain `label-field-no-options` (`{ field }`). No reader of the closed code set exists outside `packages/formula` (grep over `packages/*/src` and `ui`), so the union's growth breaks no exhaustive consumer. `optionLabelFieldOf` and `optionlessLabelSentence` are exported from `stdlib.ts` but not from the entry (`index.ts` names its stdlib exports one by one), so they stay package-internal as claimed. Correct, and `minor` covers the widening.
5. **The shared predicate is one spelling, but it is applied to two different documents — must-fix.** `declaresOptions(def)` is `Array.isArray(def.options)`, and both `objectql/formula-option-labels.ts` (`optionFields`) and the lint pass read through it. But the evaluator's map is built from the **served** object: `engine.formulaOptionLabels` → `readerOptionLabels(schema, …)` with `schema` from `registry.getObject` (engine.ts:15057 and the read path), and `getObject` → `resolveObject` → `finishServedObject` → `resolvePicklistFieldsOnto` (registry.ts:4021, picklist-resolution.ts:165), which writes the shared list's `options: [...]` onto every field authored `picklist: '<name>'`. The lint pass reads the **authored** document: `obj.fields` of the CLI stack, and at the door `item: args.body` (runtime-authoring-gate.ts:1142), i.e. the PUT body as written. The spec declares `picklist` as the option source *in place of* inline `options`, "never with it" (field.zod.ts:1641–1657: a `select`/`radio` declares one of the two, both together refused at parse), and lint's own R8 rule names a `picklist` reference as an options source (data-model-rules.ts:800–811). So for an object `{ kind: { type: 'select', picklist: 'kinds' }, pf: { type: 'formula', expression: 'label(record.kind)' } }`: today the formula evaluates and reads the list's label; with this PR `declaresOptions({ type: 'select', picklist: 'kinds' })` is `false`, and `label(record.kind)` is refused `label-field-no-options` at `os validate`, `os build`, `os lint`, the save door, publish and restore, in a sentence that is false for that field ("`kind` declares no options") with a remedy ("point `label()` at a field that declares `options`") that prescribes the schema's own refusal (`options` beside `picklist`). This is exactly the mismatch the order forbade: the gate refuses a formula that evaluates fine, and the "agree by construction" claim in the changeset, the PR body and the three doc comments does not hold for the one authored shape whose options are resolved after authoring. Worse, picklist-resolution.ts's header says a served copy "written back into the metadata service by the boot bridge" may carry marked `options` beside `picklist`, so the same object could pass the gate on one path and fail it on another. No test in either new suite exercises a picklist-bound control; both fixtures declare inline `options` only. The dev's live table could not see it: the scratch package declares no picklist.
6. **Other option sources agree with the evaluator.** `optionsFrom`, `dataSource` and reference fields (which R8 also admits) are never resolved onto `options` at serve time, so the evaluator faults on `label()` over them today and the gate now refuses them: consistent, and the refusal is a true narrowing of something that already read null. A `multiselect` / `tags` / `checkboxes` with an inline list is admitted (declares options) and the evaluator's per-row list refusal stands as before. Correct.
7. **Injected system columns.** `optionFieldNames` adds injected columns that declare options (none today, `injectedColumnDefsFor`), declared names winning. Harmless and consistent with the field index. Correct.
8. **Faces that do not run the gate, reported not changed.** MCP `validate_expression` (both bridges project fields to name/type/label/required, so `optionFields` cannot be built) and Studio's live CEL lint (`fields`/`scope` only). Reported in the os-dev-report `out_of_scope_findings`; the door's 422 still reaches both. Accepted as out of scope.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/28659-label-optionless-field-refused.md`: `@objectstack/formula` minor, `@objectstack/lint` minor, `@objectstack/objectql` patch; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` on both the PR body and the changeset body; BREAKING banner; before/now/unchanged/remedy; one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. Under AGENTS.md step 3 a value the door stored and now refuses is `narrowed`, and a declared kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves; `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`'s level axis refuses `narrowed` beside an all-`patch` set. So the order's "`patch`" could not have been declared honestly; the dev's departure (option A of the open question) is right, and `objectql` at `patch` is fine because the predicate's "at least one" is PR-scoped. `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head. Consistent.

Upgrade posture: no boot or load path runs `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` (`packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`, `packages/runtime/src` have no caller); a stored object whose formula calls `label()` on an optionless field still loads, registers and reads `null` per row with the WARN, exactly as today, and is refused only on its next active save, publish or restore, naming the field. For an optionless field that is the right disposition: the formula never worked, no conversion can give it a label. For a **picklist-bound** field (①.5) the same posture turns a working stored formula into one that cannot be re-saved, published or restored, which is an upgrade hazard the disposition does not cover; the must-fix below removes it rather than prescribing a migration.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions[0]` (changeset level): answered A in ② — minor + `narrowed` stands.
- Dev flag "two faces do not run the gate" (MCP `validate_expression`, Studio live lint): accepted as reported out-of-scope findings; the seat files the MCP one as a card (class b, seam `ExprSchemaHint.optionFields` → `mcp-http-tools validate_expression`) or records why not.
- Dev flag "multi-value selects admitted, evaluator's existing verdict": agreed, not a narrowing here.
- Not flagged by the dev, raised here: the picklist-bound shape (①.5). The PR body's "`label()` on a field that declares options (a `select`, `multiselect`, `radio`, any type with an `options` list) is admitted" is true only of inline lists; the spec's other option source is refused.
- Not flagged: the restore door runs the gate too (protocol-authoring-gate.ts:138). Acceptable, but the changeset's face list should name it or say "every door that runs the active authoring gate".
- File surface past the claim: `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts` is the body of the gate `authoring-rules.ts` runs (the claim named the wrong file, not the wrong gate); `packages/objectql/src/formula-option-labels.ts` is the one-predicate reuse the order asked for; the docs sentence is a prose face for the seat's ACCEPT. All in a sensible scope. `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.test.ts` excuses two plumbing locals in the #5017 receiver meta-test; the one metadata key read (`options`) goes through `declaresOptions`, so the meta-test's intent holds.
- Overlap: seat 1's #28679 merge commit `c946cb95914cf0a33ce1076268d1cefafe0415a3` is an ancestor of this head (merged in `0cd20573`, clean). Open #28712 (#28660) touches `packages/formula/src/stdlib.ts` in `toDate` / `addDaysUtc` / `addMonthsUtc` (no hunk overlap with `optionLabelFieldOf` / `declaresOptions` / `optionLabelOf`) and the **same line** of `packages/formula/src/index.ts` (the `from './stdlib'` export statement: `isUnparseableDate` there, `declaresOptions` here). Whichever lands second takes a one-line textual conflict with a trivial resolution (both names on the one line). The seat should expect a rebase on the second.
- Author: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; the dev session is `session_01FEkQ5pQB2Jwsce3RvocUcS` on branch `claude/project-thread-m6mfzr`. No human login to name.
- Ablation and controls (read, not re-run): red-first on base with the six source files swapped (formula 7 failed / 30 passed, lint 8 failed / 4 passed), ablation by `ablation-replace.mjs` anchor (blob `e7327b51ea43` → `991a89c6da33`, formula 5 failed / 6 passed, lint 8 failed / 4 passed, restored to HEAD, marker absent). The ablation's DTS step failed (lost narrowing) while the JS bundle the suites read carried the marker; a discarded earlier leg read a stale `dist/`. Acceptable evidence for "the check is load-bearing"; it says nothing about ①.5 because no picklist control exists.
- CI at 2026-11-01T15:10Z on head `0cd20573`: 14 check-runs concluded success (Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, PR-body guards, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Spec property liveness, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected, Auto Label, Plan Test Core shards, filter), 7 skipped by design, 0 failed, and 22 still in progress (Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Test Core 1–8, Type Check ×4, Lint ×6, Live E2E UI). Not all green yet; the landing-time ② check must be re-read from the API. No signature to compare against base since nothing is red.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published spec on `main`: `FieldSchema` (field.zod.ts) declares two option sources for a `select` / `radio`, inline `options` or a `picklist` reference, mutually exclusive, and `PicklistServedFieldSchema` declares the served form with the list's options resolved on. `label()`'s doc contract (formulas.mdx, `cel-predicates-formulas.json`, the `label` macro's own header) is "a field that declares `options`", and `translateObject` reads a picklist-bound field's options off the served form with the list's labels inherited, so at evaluation a picklist-bound select is a field `label()` answers on. The PR makes the spec's own refusal real for the inline case (a text field has no label to read: the refusal is true and the remedy works) but takes a declared capability away for the picklist case: an author following field.zod.ts's own instruction ("instead of `options`") can no longer save, publish or restore a formula that labels that field, and the sentence they read is false for their field. The one-predicate design is right; the predicate's input is wrong on one side. The fix is small and local to the lint pass (the authored document is the only place the two sides differ), with a control pinning the picklist-bound shape at all four faces, and the three "agree by construction" comments plus the changeset's "any type with an `options` list" sentence restated to name both sources.

Must-fix:
1. `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts` `optionFieldNames`: admit a field that names a picklist (`typeof f.picklist === 'string' && f.picklist !== ''`, the R8 reading in `data-model-rules.ts`) beside `declaresOptions(f)`, so the gate refuses exactly the fields the served object has no `options` for. Either widen the shared predicate so it holds on both the authored and the served form (a picklist arm beside the `options` arm; on the served form both hold, and `labelMap` still reads only `def.options`, so the evaluator's map is unchanged) or compose it in lint with the picklist arm, with a comment saying why the authored form needs it. Add a control to `runtime-gate.object-formula-label-target.test.ts` and `validate-option-label-target.test.ts`: `select` with `picklist:` and no `options`, `label(record.that)` admitted at `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint` and the door; keep the text-field LIT red. Restate the changeset's "Unchanged" bullet, the PR body's "declares options" list and the `declaresOptions` / `optionFields` doc comments to name the picklist source; `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx`'s new sentence should say "a field that declares `options` or names a `picklist`" (seat's prose ACCEPT).
